cards.explanation: The answer is that Jesus had often met there with His disciples. John 18:2 says Judas, His betrayer, knew the place because Jesus had often met there with His disciples. That's the reason the text gives. Then in verse 3 Judas brings the soldiers and officers to the garden. I think that stings a little extra, friends.

The officers are from the chief priests and Pharisees. John 18:3 says Judas brought a band of soldiers and officers from the chief priests and Pharisees. They arrived at the garden carrying lanterns, torches, and weapons. That's quite a crowd, friends.

The answer is True. John 18:3 says they arrived carrying lanterns, torches, and weapons. That's not a casual walk in the garden, bakers. They came with light and they came ready. Think of someone showing up to pick up one cookie box with a whole moving crew.

Jesus steps forward and asks who they are looking for. John 18:4 says Jesus, knowing all that was coming upon Him, stepped forward and asked, "Whom are you seeking?" He doesn't run and He doesn't hide. He steps forward. I'll be honest, friends, I once hid from a smoke alarm. This is a different level.

The answer is False. The soldiers and officers answer, "Jesus of Nazareth…" and Jesus says, "I am He." (John 18:5) He owns it right there, no wrong man, no excuses. Most of us would have at least coughed and looked around first, bakers.

The answer is True. John 18:6 says when Jesus said, "I am He," they drew back and fell to the ground. The ones who came with weapons are the ones on the floor. I think I'd have dropped my whole tray of cookies, friends.

Jesus says to let the disciples go. In John 18:8 He says, "So if you are looking for Me, let these men go." He's the one they came for, and He speaks up for the men with Him. Right there in the middle of all those torches, friends, He's thinking of them.

The word is "I have not lost one of those You have given Me." (John 18:9) The writer says Jesus speaking up for His disciples fulfills that word He had spoken. Not one of them lost, bakers. That's a word with some weight to it.
The answer is False. Jesus tells Peter, "Put your sword back in its sheath!" (John 18:11) That's the opposite of keeping it out, friends. Peter had already swung it once, and Jesus tells him to stop.

The answer is Father. Jesus says, "Shall I not drink the cup the Father has given Me?" (John 18:11) Peter has just swung a sword and taken off a man's ear, and Jesus answers by pointing to the Father. I think that tells us Jesus isn't surprised by what's happening, bakers. John 18:4 says He knew all that was coming upon Him.
